overview.title: Beneath the Atlas cedars
overview.p1: The cedar forests around Ifrane are among the defining landscapes of the Middle Atlas: towering cedars, cool shade, and forest roads. Barbary macaques may appear — do not feed them.
overview.p2: Stay on marked trails. The Cèdre Gouraud area is a well-known stop.

food.title: Eating near Cedar Forest
food.p1: Picnicking is the usual style under the cedars. Head to Ifrane or Azrou for full meals.
food.p2: Leave no food scraps in the forest and do not feed wildlife.
food.li3: Meals in Ifrane after your trail.
food.li5: Take all trash back to town.

1.title: Trails
1.desc: Wear closed-toe shoes; the ground can be uneven.

2.title: Wildlife
2.desc: Do not feed the monkeys; keep food stored away.

3.title: Weather
3.desc: Fog and cold can roll in quickly — bring a warm layer.

q1.question: Is the forest free to visit?
q1.answer: Public trails are generally free; respect any marked private or protected zones.

q2.question: Is there a famous cedar tree?
q2.answer: The area is renowned for giant Atlas cedars, including historic specimens.

q3.question: Can I combine it with the lakes?
q3.answer: Yes — it makes a classic nature day out.

q4.question: Is it suitable for children?
q4.answer: Yes, on short and easy trails.

q5.question: Does the road continue toward Azrou?
q5.answer: Yes, the cedar road continues toward Azrou — a very popular scenic loop.
